# Final report

## Outcome

The submitted edit changes only the last layer (`fc.weight`, `fc.bias`). On the practice images it raises worst-group accuracy from 72.9% to 92.5% while the weighted mean goes from 97.7% to 95.7%, confirmed by the final forward pass. Held-out, the same recipe gives the same numbers, and it beats DFR's held-out worst group by about 3.4 points.

| | landbird/land | landbird/water | waterbird/land | waterbird/water | worst | weighted mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original | 99.36 | 82.62 | 72.93 | 96.24 | 72.93 | 97.72 |
| **Submitted edit (final pass)** | 96.79 | 93.35 | 93.23 | 92.48 | **92.48** | **95.67** |
| Same recipe, 10-fold held-out, through the tool | 96.79 | 93.35 | 93.23 | 92.48 | 92.48 | 95.67 |
| DFR recipe, 10-fold held-out, through the tool | 95.72 | 89.06 | 92.48 | 95.49 | 89.06 | 95.37 |
| DFR as given (in-sample, seed average) | 97.1 | 92.2 | 100.0 | 99.4 | 92.2 | 97.4 |

- **Paired against the original:** 52 landbird/water and 27 waterbird/land images fixed, 2 and 0 broken; cost 12 landbird/land and 5 waterbird/water images.
- **Paired against held-out DFR:** the edit wins landbird/water 23 to 3 and landbird/land 10 to 5; waterbird/land is even (3 to 2); DFR wins waterbird/water 4 to 0.
- **Expectation for the test split:** about 96.8 / 93.4 / 93.2 / 94.0, i.e. worst group about 93% and mean about 96%. Drawing test-sized groups from the held-out predictions, the edit beats DFR on worst group in every draw and on the mean in about 92% of draws.
- **Uncertainty:** roughly ±1 point on landbird/water and ±1.5 on each waterbird group. The targets (88% / 94%) are met in essentially all simulated draws.

The test expectation reweights three species to their test share; see "Limits" for why that matters.

## What I changed

The new read-out is built in closed form from the four group means of the 2,048 pooled features, taken over the practice images in normal and mirrored view:

- **Direction:** the waterbird-minus-landbird mean difference, with its component along the water-minus-land mean difference removed, scaled so the bird is worth 16 logits as in the original model.
- **Over-cancellation:** I subtract a further 10% of the original background read-out, so a water background now moves the margin by −0.8 logits instead of +8.1.
- **Bias:** the midpoint between the two class means, shifted 0.25 logits toward "landbird".

The 10% and the −0.25 were chosen by cross-validation from a broad ridge, not from in-sample accuracy.

## What goes wrong in the network

- **The margin adds bird and background evidence.** The bird is worth 16.0 logits and a water background 8.1, with within-group spread about 5; that is enough to flip mismatched images.
- **The background enters layer4 as one direction.** Hiding the water-minus-land direction of layer3's output from layer4.0's two 1×1 convolutions removes 84% of the background effect (8.08 → 1.33) and leaves the bird effect at 15.9.
- **The last block amplifies two input coordinates.**
  - Cutting the scene direction at `layer4.2.conv1` takes the block's background write from +4.73 to −0.18 logits; the bird write stays at 13.9.
  - Cutting the bird direction at the same place takes the bird write from 13.9 to 2.0 and turns the model into a scene classifier (98.5% on matched groups, 19% and 35% on mismatched).
  - Doubling the gain on the bird coordinate doubles the bird effect and the spread together, so the block is linear in it.
- **fc reads the rest through the skip path.** With the layer4.2 cut in place, 3.3 logits of background effect remain, exactly the skip-path share.

Share of the background effect removed by a single cut at each site (the cuts overlap, because each block re-reads the scene code):

| Site | Removed |
|---|---|
| layer4.0's readers of layer3 | 84% |
| layer4.1's reader | 33% |
| layer4.2's reader | 61% |
| fc | 100% |

## Causal evidence for the edit

**Dose-response through the tool**, moving along the line from the original read-out to the edit:

| Fraction of the edit | 0 | 0.5 | 1 (submitted) | 1.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Worst group | 72.9 | 87.2 | 92.5 | 88.7 |
| Weighted mean | 97.7 | 97.2 | 95.7 | 89.1 |

At 1.5 the shortcut reverses: the formerly easy groups become the hard ones.

**Dose-response inside the network** (layer4.2 reader cut, fc untouched): at strengths 0 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 the block's background write is +4.73 / +2.23 / −0.18 / −5.74. An equally large cut along a non-background direction changes nothing (99.4 / 83.3 / 72.2 / 96.2).

**Counterfactual surrounds.** I pasted the central box of every practice image into one land-background and one water-background donor (1,199 pairs):

| | Prediction flips with surround | Surround effect (logits) |
|---|---|---|
| Original | 18.4% | +7.23 ± 0.12 |
| Submitted edit | 5.4% | −0.20 ± 0.09 |
| DFR as given (two seeds) | 7.6–8.3% | +0.6 to +0.8 |

For the edit, changing donor type moves the margin no more than changing to another donor of the same type, so what remains is donor-specific content. Donors are natural images, so parts of the donor's own bird sometimes stay visible and inflate all the flip rates.

**Bird-free scenes (60 land, 60 water).** The original separates them by 12.3 logits and calls 49 of 60 water scenes "waterbird" against 1 of 60 land scenes. Under the edit the gap is 2.6 logits (33 of 60 against 11 of 60), so some scene response remains when there is no bird at all.

**Other views of the same images.** Worst group is 92.5–94.0 on mirrored, shifted and ±6% zoomed versions, and 91.0 and 91.7 under 12.5% zoom-out and 14% zoom-in; the mean stays between 95.5 and 96.0.

## How I chose it, and what did not help

- **DFR's real level.** Re-running the DFR recipe inside each training fold gives about 89% worst group, not the 92–93% of its in-sample file. It separates birds as well as anything on water backgrounds, but it is about 3 points worse on land backgrounds and its threshold leans toward "waterbird".
- **Every closed-form read-out sits on one plateau.** The original direction with the background removed, the practice bird direction, and lightly whitened versions all give land-pair AUC 0.985–0.987 and water-pair AUC 0.975–0.977. The plain practice bird direction was slightly ahead of the original-anchored one and is the simplest, so I used it.
- **No in-network edit beats the read-out edit.** I ran all seven prior in-network submissions and re-derived a read-out on each one's features; differences from the fc-only edit were at most 0.003 AUC and not consistent. My own test — cutting 2, 4 or 8 surround directions at layer4.2's reader — changed AUC by less than 0.001.
- **Other ideas that gave nothing:**
  - clamping the scene coordinate to its land value at layer4.2's reader;
  - lowering the last block's thresholds;
  - doubling the bird gain;
  - whitening by view noise;
  - a read-out fitted on water-background images only;
  - a towhee-specific boost.
- **Over-cancelling by 10% is a modest, assumption-dependent gain.** A bootstrap puts it at +0.6 ± 0.4 points of expected worst group over exact cancellation, for 0.3 points of mean. On held-out halves with plain practice weighting the gain shrinks to +0.3 ± 0.8.
- **Finer tuning is noise.** When I repeated the whole selection on half the images and scored the other half, adaptive selection did no better than fixed settings, so I stopped optimising.

## Limits

- **The remaining errors are recognition failures, not background.**
  - Feature maps of the landbird/water errors show almost no landbird votes on the pasted bird; correct landbirds have 10–13 strongly negative cells, the errors fewer than one.
  - Clipping per-cell votes fixes 0 of 31.
  - Moved onto new backgrounds, about 25 of the 31 error crops are still called waterbird.
  - About half of these images contain a second animal or person in the water photo (ducks, geese, a merganser, sea lions, surfers).
- **Three songbird species carry the "waterbird" label.** Pewee-like flycatchers (8 practice images) are wrong under every read-out including DFR; towhees are about 5 of 7 right; meadowlarks are right. They account for 10 of the 19 waterbird errors.
- **The test expectation depends on species mix.** I assume each of these species is about 2.3% of each test waterbird group, where practice has 3.8% pewees in waterbird/water. That assumption is from my knowledge of the dataset, not something I could check here. If the test mix is like practice, waterbird/water is about 92.5 instead of 94.
- **DFR is better on waterbird/water.** Its held-out score there is about 3 points higher, bought with a threshold that costs it 4 points on landbird/water.
- **Bird size shifts the operating point slightly.** With birds 12.5% smaller, waterbird/land drops to 91.0.
- **No pristine holdout exists.** Every practice image was used at some point. The held-out figures are cross-validated, and other views of images a read-out was fitted on are not independent — DFR stays at 97–98% on them.

All 50 passes are used. The submitted tensors are in `work/edited`, with identical copies in `work/best_1` and `work/best_final`; the full log is in `work/notes.md`.
